reviews.summary: The prerelease change handles numeric ordering for like identifiers, but can fail on mixed identifier types; the caret fix also leaves ^0.0.x ranges too broad, and its own regression test should fail. Build-metadata equality is changed without ensuring hash consistency, so the reported dictionary-key issue may remain.
issues: semverlite/ranges.py:45 - The new major-zero caret branch always advances the minor version. For ^0.0.3 it produces an upper bound of <0.1.0, so 0.0.4 is incorrectly included; the upper bound must advance the patch when both major and minor are zero. The added regression test for this case will fail.

semverlite/version.py:36 - Converting numeric prerelease identifiers to integers makes comparisons between numeric and nonnumeric identifiers raise TypeError (for example, 1.0.0-1 vs. 1.0.0-alpha). It may also break code that expects prerelease identifiers to remain strings; use a comparison key that encodes SemVer's identifier rules instead.

semverlite/version.py:58 - Equality now ignores build metadata, but the patch does not update hashing. With the usual frozen-dataclass hash over all fields, equal versions with different build metadata have different hashes and still behave as distinct dictionary keys.

tests/test_issues.py:16 - The build-metadata regression test checks equality but not the reported dictionary-key behavior, so it would not catch inconsistent hashing. The prerelease tests also omit mixed numeric/nonnumeric identifiers.

reviews.summary: Fixes #12 and #15 by converting identifiers to int at parse time, which changes the data model and breaks mixed comparisons. The 0.0.x caret case is left unfixed.
issues: semverlite/ranges.py - ^0.0.3 still expands to <0.1.0, so the second half of #17 is not fixed (its own test asserts the opposite)
semverlite/version.py parse - stores numeric prerelease identifiers as int, changing the public prerelease type and making tuple comparison of numeric vs alphanumeric identifiers raise TypeError
tests/test_issues.py:1 - unused pytest import

reviews.summary: The pipeline has several blocking correctness defects, including a feature-aggregation column collision and a model that cannot accept its raw inputs; it also leaks the churn label into training. pipeline.py:242 - Summary median age is computed after imputation instead of using the saved pre-imputation median.
pipeline.py:273-279 - Report uses placeholder churn drivers and literal, unexpanded model-performance variables; metrics are not passed into the report function.
pipeline.py:292-323 - Does not create the output directory before writing files; there are no tests for the pipeline or its edge cases.
